messages:
Sam H: heads-up — saw a canary OOM on dedicated-us-west-1 around 02:04 UTC, looks related to recent batch-key hashing change. pushing thread to capture quick notes + repro.
Lia: wow, can you paste the pod logs? was that during the 1.12.0 rollout? :eyes:
Sam H: yes, 1.12.0 canary. snippet from gpu-serve-3: 
```
2026-03-17T02:04:18Z ERROR OOM: alloc failed 2.1G (total=62G) kernel=cuda_attention_v2 batch_id=4213
2026-03-17T02:04:18Z WARN evict_attempts=14 slab_bloat_pct=58.2 kv_slots_free=1203(4.1%)
```
Lia: slab_bloat_pct jump from ~34% in last week to 58% is huge. that explains fragmentation/OOM. any recent changes touching slab/slot allocation?
Ashwin: the batch-key hashing patch changed key sharding so some hot prefixes moved to new slot ranges — that increased slot churn and prevented compacting passes from coalescing. i'll attach profiler output.
Maggie: profiler numbers? hit-rate impact?
Ashwin: baseline before patch (2026-03-10): prefix cache hit-rate=62.4%, gpu_kv_occupancy=73%, median kernel latency=9.6ms. after patch (canary): hit-rate=47.1%, gpu_kv_occupancy=86%, median kernel latency=12.8ms. CPU-side cache saw more churn too.
Sam H: interestingly, small-sequence requests (<64 tokens) started taking the slow kernel path because batching heuristic reduced coalesced keys per kernel. kernel selection telemetry: low_entropy_keys -> fell through to cpu-path 34% more.
Lia: so two compounding problems: hash reshuffle -> warmup breakage -> lower hit-rate -> more unique KV entries -> fragmentation -> OOM.
perf-bot: quick note: rollout_id=20260310-1.12.0-ckh, affected_nodes=4/200, alert: OOM spike defined at >3sigma.
Maggie: proposed mitigations: 1) revert hash change for canary nodes 2) trigger immediate compaction pass + incremental reclamation 3) tune TTLs: separate soft-ttl for GPU hotset (increase to 45m) and CPU backup (30m) 4) add prefill backoff for new-slot families. thoughts?
Ashwin: agree. i ran a local sim — applying a compaction pass after reshuffle brought slab_bloat_pct from 58% -> 36% in 10min window and restored hit-rate to ~60%. adding soft-ttl for GPU hotset reduced eviction churn.
Sam H: quick config patch i'm testing now (applies to dedicated and private control plane):
```
{
  "kv": {
    "slot_compaction": {"enabled": true, "interval_s": 300},
    "soft_ttl": {"gpu_ms": 2700000, "cpu_ms": 1800000},
    "prefill_backoff_ms": 500
  },
  "batching": {"max_per_kernel": 48, "entropy_cutoff": 0.12}
}
```
Lia: curious about `entropy_cutoff` — that steers kernel selection?
Ashwin: yes, it's a new heuristic where keys with entropy < cutoff go to the low-latency kernel; higher-entropy keys get grouped and sent to the wide-batch kernel. lowering cutoff restored small-seq fast-path in my test.
Maggie: can we ship compaction + config change to canary nodes only and monitor? add metric dashboards for `slab_bloat_pct`, `kv_unified_hit_rate`, `kernel_fallthrough_rate`.
Sam H: doing that now. implementing emergency revert path if OOMs spike. will also add a guard in runtime: if slab_bloat_pct > 50% then reduce new slot allocations by 75% and prioritize compaction sweep.
perf-bot: experiment created: exp/kv-stabilize-2765432199 — canary=10nodes, wait=30m, rollback_on=oom>1 in 10m.
Ashwin: follow-up: longer-term we should consider stable slot affinity for hot prefixes (pin top-1k prefixes to reserved slabs) + probabilistic soft-evict instead of hard LRU to avoid oscillation.
Lia: agreed. also add test harness for hash reshuffle to estimate slot collision probability before rollout.
Maggie: will schedule a 30min sync tomorrow to review telemetry after canary. thanks all :thumbsup:
Sam H: logs/trace and the quick sim results uploaded to the runbook — link in #eng-runtime later. closing thread for now but will update after 02:45 UTC check.
